name: nifty_banknifty_spread_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: BANK NIFTY carries ~33% weight in NIFTY 50, creating a tight but imperfect correlation. The intraday return spread between BANK NIFTY and NIFTY 50 exhibits mean-reverting behavior around a slowly drifting mean. When BANK NIFTY outperforms NIFTY 50 by > 30 bps intraday (or vice versa), the spread tends to compress over the next 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because: (1) BANK NIFTY is the most traded F&O instrument and attracts speculative overreaction, (2) passive index funds rebalance toward NIFTY 50 weights, creating a natural reversion mechanism, (3) the spread is only mean-reverting intraday — overnight the spread can shift permanently based on macro factors. We trade this as a spread trade using NIFTY and BANK NIFTY futures (or their most liquid ETFs).
stock_filter: Trade via NIFTY 50 futures + BANK NIFTY futures (or NIFTYBEES + BANKBEES ETFs)

conditions: nb_spread_zscore < -1.5 (NIFTY outperforming BANK NIFTY — expect BANK NIFTY catch-up)
spread_velocity < -3 (spread still widening — wait for it to slow)
nb_spread_zscore > 1.5 (BANK NIFTY outperforming NIFTY — expect compression)

entry.entry_price: market order on both legs: long BANK NIFTY + short NIFTY (or vice versa)

exit.stop_loss: nb_spread_zscore extends to ±2.5 (spread diverging beyond threshold)
exit.time_stop: exit after 60 bars if target not reached
exit.signal_exit: India_VIX spikes > 22 during trade (correlation structure may break)

risk.position_sizing: ₹50K per leg, beta-adjusted (multiply NIFTY leg by BANK NIFTY beta to NIFTY, ~1.3)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; in high VIX, BANK NIFTY drops faster (higher beta) and spread may not revert
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 15 min or last 10 min
filters.volume_filter: both futures trading at > 0.8x normal volume participation
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 intraday move > 1.5% (strong trend makes spread directional, not mean-reverting)
filters.spread_filter: futures bid-ask spread < 0.05% on both legs
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day (banking-specific), budget day, F&O expiry
other_filters: skip if HDFC Bank/ICICI Bank have results today (distorts BANK NIFTY)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — NIFTY/BANK NIFTY spread mean reversion is structural due to the weight overlap and passive fund rebalancing. This trade has been viable for years in Indian markets.

weaknesses: On RBI policy days or banking-specific regulatory events, BANK NIFTY diverges from NIFTY permanently intraday. The stop loss at z-score ±2.5 gets hit on such days.
Trading two index futures requires significant margin (especially BANK NIFTY at ~₹10L notional). The ₹1L capital allocation may be insufficient for proper sizing.
The beta-adjustment ratio between BANK NIFTY and NIFTY is time-varying (1.2-1.5) and using a stale beta leads to imperfect hedging.
prior_art: Vidyamurthy (2004) 'Pairs Trading: Quantitative Methods and Analysis' — seminal text on spread trading. Elliot, van der Hoek & Malcolm (2005) 'Pairs Trading' for mean-reverting spread models. In India, the NIFTY/BANK NIFTY spread is widely discussed but typically traded on daily charts, not intraday.
notes: Consider using options for the spread trade: buy BANK NIFTY calls + NIFTY puts (or vice versa) to limit downside risk. This converts the trade from a spread trade to a relative volatility trade but caps the loss at premium paid.
